style: High-tempo attacking football under Rudi Garcia, blending veterans with emerging talent; creativity through De Bruyne and pace via Doku.
recent_form: Qualified with De Bruyne and Doku leading the goal output; arrived ranked ninth as a fading-golden-generation side in transition.

key_players.name: Kevin De Bruyne
key_players.note: Chief playmaker; led qualifying with six goals and remains the team's creative hub.

key_players.name: Jeremy Doku
key_players.note: Explosive one-v-one dribbler; added five goals in qualification.

key_players.name: Romelu Lukaku
key_players.note: All-time top scorer (89 goals) at his fourth World Cup; the central finishing reference.

key_players.name: Thibaut Courtois
key_players.note: World-class shot-stopper capable of winning matches on his own.

key_players.name: Leandro Trossard
key_players.note: Arsenal attacker providing flexibility and end product across the front line.

key_players.name: Youri Tielemans
key_players.note: Aston Villa midfielder offering passing range and balance in the centre.

historical_news: Golden generation reached the 2018 World Cup semi-finals (third place), their best finish.
Underwhelming 2022 group-stage exit triggered a squad transition.
Rudi Garcia tasked with blending ageing stars and new talent.
Reliance on De Bruyne and Lukaku as the generation's final tournament window.
Long-standing 'best team never to win' narrative around the golden generation.

media_sentiment.label: neutral
media_sentiment.summary: Seen as a quality but declining side capable of a run if veterans stay fit, no longer a top favourite.
